Look at any picture of Krishna. There's always one thing on his head. Not a crown of gold. A peacock feather. Why? As the story goes, it started in a forest in Vrindavan.
Young Krishna sits on a rock and plays his flute. And the whole forest goes quiet. The birds stop singing. The cows stop chewing.
Then the peacocks come. One. Ten. A hundred. And they start to dance. Tails open, spinning, shimmering, for hours.
Wait, so who gives a gift to God? When the music ends, the king of the peacocks walks up, bows, and drops one perfect feather at his feet.
Krishna picks it up, smiles, and tucks it into his hair. And he never takes it off.
That's why, even today, his crown carries a feather, and so many homes keep one near the altar. Not gold. A gift from a friend. Comment Mor Pankh if you have one at home.
